One grey, wind-scoured afternoon, as he collected driftwood along the high tide line, he spotted a sealed glass bottle half-buried in warm sand. Inside, a crumpled note written in smudged blue ink: “If you find this, tell my granddaughter I never stopped thinking of her.” His throat tightened; he tucked the note into his wool coat, knowing he would spend weeks searching for the girl, carrying that fragile, decades-old message across miles of wind and rain.", "w02": "凌晨四点的城市褪去了白日的喧嚣，主干道上的车流稀稀拉拉，路边的便利店亮着暖黄的灯，偶尔有晚归的代驾骑手骑着电动车掠过，带起一阵细碎的风。行道树的影子在路灯下拉得很长，小区门口的保安室里飘出淡淡的茶香，远处的天际线还蒙着一层浅灰的雾，没有早高峰的拥挤，没有商铺的叫卖声，整座城市像刚从睡梦里醒转，软乎乎地裹在清凉的夜色余温里，等着第一缕阳光落下来。", "w03": "- Think of recursion like two identical mirrors facing each other: you see your reflection, then a smaller reflection of you, then an even smaller one, repeating until the images fade from view.\n- Every repeated small step gets you closer to a simple end point, like counting down from ten by saying “ten, nine, eight…” until you hit zero and stop.\n- Recursion never goes on forever, because there is always a clear stop rule, just like you don’t keep counting below zero when you reach the end point."}
